title: A White repertoire: reasons you can say, moves you must know
outcomes: Builds a short White repertoire from the replies his own opponents actually play, with a plan sentence for each
Separates forcing positions, where an exact move is worth remembering, from flexible ones, where the plan is worth understanding
Chooses among several sound moves by the plan he can state

steps.text: A repertoire is a short list of replies to what you actually meet. Start from your own games, not from a book. Write the first three or four moves of your last ten games as White. Count which positions repeat, and build your White replies for the two you meet most.

steps.prompt: From your last ten games as White: which two positions come up most? Write them down. Which one will you prepare first, and why that one?

steps.text: Two kinds of position. In a **forcing** position, one slip loses at once, so an exact move is worth remembering and revisiting. In a **flexible** position many moves work, so learn the plan, not the move order. Spend memory on the first kind and understanding on the second.

steps.title: Memorise or understand?
steps.prompt: In which position would remembering one exact move pay? Predict, then check.

steps.text: **When it holds.** Rule of thumb: if the natural move loses a lot, remember the exact move; if several moves stay close, remember the plan. **When it fails.** You cannot tell from the look of a position which kind it is, and a plan you cannot state is not understanding. Ask: what does this move do?

steps.prompt: Pick one White reply you chose today. Write its plan in one sentence without naming a move. Then write one position where you would need to remember an exact move.

sources: items IA4-141, IA4-144, IA4-145, IG-ENDMATE-23, ISsp12-1..5 (engine depth 16, checked by tools/validate.py)
